The hosted XNU drives the CPU and MMU directly, so macOS processes run natively next to Linux processes on the same CPUs, with no hypervisor between them. Linux lends XNU its memory, timers, files, network and GPU through a small interface module (fki.ko).

new.readme: Three complete LLM projects written in 100% pure x86-64 NASM assembly. Zero C, zero C++, zero Rust, zero libc, zero libm, zero runtime dependencies. Assembled directly with nasm and linked with ld. Every math kernel (expf, sincosf, RMSNorm, RoPE, SiLU, Softmax), AVX2+FMA+F16C GEMM/GEMV engine, BPE tokenizer, clone()/futex() thread pool, bare-metal SMP kernel, analytical backward pass, AdamW optimizer, and live Unicode Braille TUI is hand-written x86-64 assembly (17,252 lines total across all three projects).

new.description: A training engine for your local model, using your idle compute
new.readme: A training engine for your local model, using your idle compute. Songe is a training engine for the model you already run locally. It sits between your agent and your model server as an OpenAI-compatible proxy, logs how each of the model's actions turned out, and fine-tunes a LoRA adapter on those lessons while the agent is idle. A new version is served only if it does clearly better than the one in use, and everything stays on your machine unless you enable the optional cloud learning.

items.harder: Overseas data centers that remotely supply significant compute to companies headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau face new export restrictions, and chip exporters, foundries and data centers must perform due diligence on customers.

items.title: One approval can cover a coordinated frontend and backend change routed through T3 Code
items.connection: On 2026-11-23 Magpie suggested approval gates get one checkpoint when all agent coding flows through T3 Code; today's multi-repo turns in T3 Code 0.1.12 mean a change spanning several repositories also arrives as one turn on that path, so one gate covers the whole change.
items.context: Cross-repo changes are a common source of broken releases
chain: An orchestrator already routes all coding to T3 Code over one MCP link.
Before, a frontend, backend and library change became separate turns and separate approvals that could be merged out of step.
Now the approver sees the coordinated change in one turn and approves or rejects it together.
Fewer half-merged changes reach staging, and teams can keep libraries in separate repos without a heavier review process.
items.who: Engineering leads approving agent work benefit; product teams with split frontend, backend and shared library repos would pay.
items.variable: cross-repo changes merged out of step per month
items.versus: Separate per-repo approvals let one side merge before the other, and a monorepo migration is far more costly.
items.smallest_test: Route 10 known cross-repo tasks through T3 Code with one approval gate; success if at least 8 arrive as a single reviewable turn and none merge partially.
items.disconfirm: Multi-repo turns still produce separate branches the approver must handle one by one, or conflicts force manual splitting.

items.context: Enterprises pick tooling on measured fit rather than popularity
chain: Hurdle gives an open npm harness that scores real coding agents on skill and docs tasks.
Stitch-skills claims its open-standard skills work across multiple coding agents, but stars do not show whether they do.
Maintainers can publish a per-agent pass table for each skill and flag those that only work in one agent.
Platform teams can then approve a skill library for mixed Claude Code and Codex fleets on evidence, which shortens internal tooling reviews.
items.who: Skill library maintainers and internal developer platform teams benefit; platform teams running mixed agent fleets would pay for a maintained portability report.
items.variable: share of skills passing on both agents
items.versus: Without a scored run, teams learn a skill breaks in one agent only after developers hit it in real work.
items.smallest_test: Wrap 10 stitch-skills tasks in Hurdle and run each 5 times on Claude Code and Codex; success if the harness separates skills that pass on both agents from skills that pass on one, with at least 2 skills showing a gap.
items.disconfirm: Pass rates are equal across agents for every skill, or run-to-run variance is larger than the gap between agents.

items.lead: Local inference cuts conversion and runtime overhead on consumer hardware.
items.body: In llama.cpp, Inkling 2 Mini now serves natively from its NVFP4 GGUF across Apple Silicon, CUDA, AMD, Windows, and Vulkan, while llm.asm runs Qwen3-0.6B in 12 KB of zero-dependency x86-64 assembly. Avoiding requantization preserves native accuracy, and stripping runtime and OS layers shows how much CPU decode speed can be recovered. llama.cpp lacks throughput and memory-bandwidth benchmarks, and llm.asm's speed claims are author-reported on x86-64 only.

items.lead: Coding agents gain multi-repo scope as simulation testing moves to one standard.
items.body: In T3 Code 0.1.12, one agent turn can now span several repositories, while Real2SimLab evaluates coding agents generating simulation programs from video on one platform. That removes manual switching across frontend, backend, and library repos, and makes simulation benchmarks comparable. T3 Code omits conflict handling, branch coordination, and context limits, and Real2SimLab offers only a paper summary without code or scores.
